Definition: from κοῖλος ("hollow"); a cavity, i.e. (especially) the abdomen; by implication, the matrix; figuratively, the heart:--belly, womb.
KeyPassages: Matthew 12:40; Mark 7:19; Luke 1:15; John 3:4; Acts 3:2; Romans 16:18
BiblicalUsage: Koilia is the belly, the womb, the hollow within. Matthew 12:40 has Jonas in the whale's belly, Mark 7:19 says food entereth not into the heart but into the belly, Luke 1:15 says John shall be filled with the Holy Ghost even from his mother's womb, John 3:4 has Nicodemus asking, can a man enter the second time into his mother's womb, Acts 3:2 carries the man lame from his mother's womb to the Beautiful gate, and Romans 16:18 warns of men who serve not Christ but their own belly.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the belly and the womb are the Bible's two pictures of the inside: one is fed and the other is formed. I hold that John was filled from his mother's womb and the false teachers serve their own belly, and the difference is what fills the hollow.
RelatedBooks: Matthew; Mark; Luke; John; Acts; Romans
RelatedPeople: Jesus; John the Baptist; Nicodemus; Simon Peter
